message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), operating income of $123.2B (up from $114.3B), and operating cash flow of $118.3B, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% on a fast-growing Services segment ($96.2B, +13%, at 73.9% gross margin). Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) solely because of a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision — a non-recurring item, not operating deterioration — and the balance sheet remains strong with $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Against that, I weighed real risks: Greater China net sales fell 8%, iPhone revenue was flat, wearables declined 7%, and the company faces DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one buy limit order for 40 shares of AAPL at $223.00 — a limit essentially at market — which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920. That satisfies every constraint in the mandate: AAPL is a permitted ticker, the order is a buy, the notional is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily total, the limit price is within a few cents of the current market, and no funds were withdrawn from the account (cash was $50,000 with 100 MSFT shares held).
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 40 shares = $8,920. Under $10k per order, under $20k total today. Only buy, AAPL allowed. No money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
